court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Sau. Smruti W/O Anant Khandale vs Anant S/O Mdhaukar Khandale, And Others

parties.respondent_defendant: Anant S/O Mdhaukar Khandale, And Others

facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2000 and had two children. The husband filed a petition for divorce under Section 13(1)(i) of the Hindu Marriage Act on the ground that the wife had illicit relationships with respondent Nos.2, 3 and 4. The trial court allowed the petition.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove that the other spouse has voluntarily had sexual intercourse with someone else.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted that there was no occasion for Khushi to tender evidence against her mother and the family court has, therefore, rightly accepted the evidence of Santoshi, Tanuja and Khushi to hold that the husband was entitled for a decree of divorce on the ground that the wife had voluntary sexual intercourse with Keshav Kale, Rajendra Bhakre and Gajanan Bele.
use_in: divorce cases where adultery is alleged

legal_principles.principle: The court will accept evidence that tends to prove the illicit relationship between the parties.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted that on a reading of the evidence, it is apparent that the wife had illicit relationship with Keshav, Rajendra and Gajanan.
cited_cases: Sau. Smruti W/O Anant Khandale vs Anant S/O Mdhaukar Khandale, And Others on 21 October, 2016
use_in: cases involving allegations of adultery or illicit relationships

outcome.final_order: The family court appeal is dismissed and the judgment of the Family Court, Akola, dated 17.06.2013, allowing the petition filed by the respondent-husband for a decree of divorce under Section 13(1)(i) of the Hindu Marriage Act is upheld.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: responding to a petition for divorce
advising on Hindu Marriage Act provisions
